name: Adaiah
overview: Adaiah was a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Bani. He is notably mentioned for having married a foreign wife, a detail that highlights the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenantal purity. There is no additional tribal or familial information recorded about him beyond this unique attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Adaiah means 'adornment of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that points to a person adorned or honored by the Lord. This proper name, found in Ezra 10:29, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation in the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Adaiah as a descendant of Bani, establishing a clear familial link. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text, and no further relational data is provided outside of his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Adaiah's mention in Ezra 10:29 serves as a representation of the post-exilic community's struggle to uphold God's covenant by separating from foreign marriages. His case exemplifies the broader narrative of repentance and restoration among the returned exiles, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness to God's commands during the rebuilding of Israel. This highlights the spiritual renewal efforts led by Ezra and the community in Jerusalem.
